correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<λ<1 and 2/3<θ<1, radial Parseval gives log M_n(s)=nF(s)+O(log(n+1)); the ratio of squared moduli is maximized at angle zero and an arc of length 2/n gives the lower bound. F(s)=4 atanh(U tanh(s/4))=Us+cs³+O(s⁵). The concave tangent at Un with slope s=θ(Un)^(θ−1) gives the upper bound. Under the tilt the shifts ±s/2 give constants 19c/8−L/2 and −7c/8−L/2 at scale ns³, both negative for L=10(c+1). The tangent deficit on |k−Un|≤Lns² is O(n^(5θ−4)), as is ns⁵. The normalizing subtraction and division by two produce exactly the claimed coefficient and remainder. The frozen finite coefficient checker was inspected, not executed; it is not the proof.

evidence: Let s=θ(Un)^(θ−1) and choose k to be the nearest integer to nF′(s). Then k−Un∼3cns²≫n^(1/3) and is o(n). The Region VII prefactor has logarithm O(log n). If F′(v)=k/n, then v−s=O(1/(ns)) since F″(s)∼6cs. The theorem gives log |a_{n,k}|²=nF(v)−vk+O(log n)=nF(s)−sk+O(log n) (the rounding error in the action is O(1/(ns))).

This single positive weighted summand gives log Z_n≥(Un)^θ−sUn+nF(s)−O(n^(5θ−4)+log n) by Taylor expansion of k^θ. Conversely the concave tangent and Parseval with the angular maximum at zero give log Z_n≤(Un)^θ−sUn+nF(s).
